title: Family seeks answers after teen's death; Port Alberni woman dies after night in jail; questions raised about her care in custody
article: The family of an 18-year-old Port Alberni woman who died after spending a night in jail is raising questions about the care she received while in police custody.
Jocelyn Nynah Marsha George was arrested June 23, held overnight in RCMP cells, and found the next morning "in need of medical attention," the B.C. Coroners Service said.
She was taken by ambulance to West Coast General Hospital in Port Alberni and then flown by air ambulance to Royal Jubilee Hospital in Victoria, where she died.

Richard Lucas, George's great uncle and chief of the Hesquiaht First Nation, said the young woman's family and band are seeking answers about "what went wrong and where, because, certainly, this wasn't a natural death."
He said George was the mother of two young children.

Lucas said it's unclear at this point whether drugs or alcohol were a factor in the young woman's death. It's believed she was arrested on the afternoon of July 23, released, then picked up again a short time later and held overnight, he said.
"It's been very difficult because we don't know how she died or why she died the way she did," he said. "How was she treated? That's what we're trying to find out."

The RCMP and the coroner's service referred questions to B.C.'s Independent Investigations Office, which is taking the lead on the case. The civilian-led agency reviews police-involved incidents that result in death or serious harm.
Office spokesman Marten Yousseff said the initial focus of the investigation "is to see if there is any connection between police action or inaction and the death of the youth."
He said investigators will be interviewing witnesses and officers and reviewing any available video footage.
